definitions.alerts: r1020_common episode semantics: frozen artifact threshold; 3600-second per-mint cooldown over the whole report chain: a day starts from carry.cooldown of the previous indexed day (its alerts of its last 3600 s; no older alert can block a row of this day), unlabelled emissions consume cooldown. Episode=(mint,t+60*(first_cross_min+1)); credit only the alert own positive crossing after issuance; an episode that crosses after midnight keeps the first alert the previous day gave it (carry.episodes). Precision excludes unlabelled alerts; recall at >=5 and >=15 minutes; false episodes/day uses calendar exposure. Committed format lacks issued_at: prediction t is the issuance proxy, so lead times are optimistic and are NOT actual delivered-alert performance.
definitions.calibration: Bands: lower [0,.02), watch [.02,.10), high [.10,1]. Deciles: ascending rank by (p,t,mint,kind), group floor(10*rank/n), ties may split. O/E=sum(y)/sum(p), null if sum(p)=0. Wilson 95% binomial interval z=1.959963984540054; descriptive only, does not adjust for correlated predictions.
definitions.chain: previous={day, sha256} of the previous indexed day report file, null on the first day. carry, per sample: cooldown=[mint, t] of the alerts selected in the last 3600 s of the day; episodes=[mint, crossing, first alert t or null] of the crash episodes crossing after the day ends. A day is recomputed from its own rows and the previous report carry; verify.py report --deep recomputes every day from the first.
definitions.grid: grid_bin(p): below 0.5 the cell of p, from 0.5 the mirrored cell of 1-p (an exact subtraction); each power-of-two interval [2^e,2^(e+1)) for e=-20..-2 is cut into 64 equal parts with math.frexp and power-of-two scaling, and below 2^-20 is one cell: 2434 cells, non-decreasing in p, the same integer on every platform (no logarithm). grid_mid(k) is the cell exact midpoint.
definitions.label: air/r1020_forward.label_day: last native bar in [t-300,t-60] with finite positive close and reserves; y=1 iff a token close in [t,t+3540] is <=0.10 times reference close. All 60 market-wide native minutes required. Sparse token trading is allowed; invalid future closes censor. first_cross_min is start-stamped offset 0..59; crossing completes one minute later.
definitions.limits: Labels are operator-supplied outcomes, not cryptographically proven market data. Recompute verifies arithmetic and prediction commitments, not the market bars, issuance time, selective feed loss, or profitability.
definitions.misses: Up to 10 labelled negatives with highest p and 10 positives with lowest p, ties by (t,mint,kind); no binary threshold implied.
definitions.partials: Per sample, over labelled SOL rows: sum_p=fsum(p); sum_brier=fsum((p-y)^2); sum_log=fsum(y*log(p)+(1-y)*log1p(-p)) with p clipped as for log loss; band_sum_p=fsum(p) per band; grid={cell: [rows, positives]}; lead_minutes={minutes from first alert to crossing: crash episodes}, "0" = no alert before the crossing; shared_with_previous_day=the same count over the episodes the previous indexed day also had, as that day counted them. A window adds them; an episode that spans midnight is counted once, as the later day saw it.
definitions.ranking: AP=sum over descending equal-score groups of (new positives / total positives)*(cumulative positives / cumulative rows); AP/prevalence=AP/crash_rate; both null without positives. ap_grid and ap_grid_over_prevalence: the same formula with the scores grouped by their grid cell (descending cells), computed exactly from the integer grid counts.
definitions.sampling: minute: all committed rows; coin_hour: first committed minute per mint and UTC hour, chosen before dropping unlabelled rows. These samples remain correlated.
definitions.scores: crash_rate=mean(y); Brier=mean((p-y)^2); baseline_brier=crash_rate*(1-crash_rate); Brier skill=1-Brier/baseline_brier, null for constant outcomes. Aggregates use their own pooled base rate. Log loss uses natural logs and p clipped to [1e-12,1-1e-12].
definitions.slope: Unpenalized logistic recalibration: logit P(y=1)=intercept+slope*logit(p), clip p to [1e-12,1-1e-12]; maximum likelihood by Newton with line search on logit(p) standardized by its weighted mean and standard deviation, from the identity recalibration (intercept 0, slope 1), at most 80 iterations, until both components of the gradient of the mean negative log-likelihood are below 1e-8; then, with their own budget, up to three undamped Newton steps, each kept unless it raises that loss by more than 1e-14, until a step is below 1e-13: the converged fit, which any solver reproduces to about 1e-9 or better. Null if fewer than 10 positive or 10 negative rows; nearly constant scores (the standard deviation of logit(p) below 1e-3 times max(1, the absolute mean)); singular information at any iterate (the determinant of the standardized mean information below 1e-16); no step among the 25 line-search sizes 1, 1/2, ..., 2^-24 with that loss at most 1e-14 above its current value; a last Newton step still above 1e-6 (a flat direction, such as separation); or no convergence within 80 iterations. Diagnostic, never a score adjustment. calibration_slope_grid and calibration_intercept_grid: the same fit on the grid cells, each cell at its exact midpoint grid_mid with its row and positive counts.
definitions.universe: Committed sol rows only. nonsol_exp counted separately, never labelled. Invalid/missing probabilities dropped. A sol row whose mint does not end in "pump" is outside the native bar universe that label_day reads (it can only return no_reference_bar there): counted as outside_label_universe, never labelled. Rows removed by the other native-filter conditions appear as no_reference_bar or no_valid_reference_bar. Missing horizons are dropped, never negative.
definitions.windows: This file covers its UTC day only. Seven calendar days ending on a day, and since the first indexed commitment day, can be composed from the daily files alone (their summaries and partials): missing calendar days add exposure but no observations, and no historical bar is re-queried or re-labelled. Every indexed day through the report day must be reported.
